newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eduscho to shift coffee plant capacity from Berlin.
newsitem.headline: Eduscho to shift coffee plant capacity from Berlin.

text.p: German coffee roaster Eduscho GmbH & Co KG, owned by Tchibo Holding AG since January, plans to shut its Berlin roasting plant by mid-1998 and shift capacity elsewhere, spokesman Rolf Helmbrecht said.
The spokesman, confirming a German trade press report, stressed this did not mean Eduscho planned to reduce its coffee production.
Eduscho last year accounted for 10 percent of Germany's roasted coffee consumption in private households of 389,000 tonnes. It carried out roasting in Berlin, Vienna and Bremen.

Helmbrecht said the move was a result of the expiry of special West Berlin tax breaks granted in the days of communist East Germany and the fact that the plant, Coffea Kaffee GmbH & Roesterei KG, was located in a residential area.
It provided 40 to 50 percent of Eduscho coffee products, specialising exclusively in whole beans.
Consumers increasingly preferred ready-ground coffee in vacuum packs, which was another reason for the move.
The plant's raw materials presently arrive from Bremen by rail.
Helmbrecht said capacity might be moved to Bremen, Vienna or existing Tchibo plants, but nothing was confirmed.
Both companies, with a combined coffee market share approaching 30 percent, say they continue to be operated as separate entities until further notice by Tchibo.
